text:
Doctor: (handing me my new born baby) I'm sorry but your wife didn't make it
Me: (handing baby back to him) Bring me the one my wife made
gist: A doctor hands a man his newborn saying his wife didn't make it, and the man hands the baby back asking for the one his wife did make.

wordplay.explanation: 'Didn't make it' means died, but is taken as 'didn't make (produce) this baby'.

characters.looks: somber doctor in scrubs, surgical cap
confused new father, hospital gown over clothes
newborn baby in blanket

adaptNote: Russian 'не выжила' has no 'make' sense; rework with 'не справилась'.

text:
A drunk guy is showing friends his new apartment...
The last stop is the bedroom, where a big brass gong sits next to the bed.
"What's that gong for?" the friend asks him.
"It's not a gong," the drunk replies. "It's a talking clock."
"How does it work?"
The guys picks up a hammer, gives the gong an ear-shattering pound, and steps back.
Suddenly, someone on the other side of the wall screams, "For God's sake, you asshole...it's 3:30 in the god damn morning!"
gist: A drunk shows off a gong as his talking clock, strikes it at night, and an angry neighbor yells the exact time through the wall.

characters.looks: tipsy man, messy hair, untucked shirt, grin
puzzled friend, casual clothes
angry voice behind the wall, pajamas

text:
We are 11 days into self-isolation ands it is really upsetting me to witness my wife standing at the living room window gazing aimlessly into space with tears running down her cheeks.
Don’t get me wrong, I empathize with her.  I’ve considered letting her in many times, but rules are rules.
gist: A husband describes his wife tearfully staring through the window during lockdown, then reveals she is outside and he won't let her in.

characters.looks: man on sofa in sweatpants, mock sympathetic face
woman outside window, tearful, pressed against glass

text:
Two young boys walked into a pharmacy, picked out a box of tampons, and proceeded to the checkout counter
The man at the counter asked the older boy, "Son, how old are you?"
"Eight" the boy replied.
The man continued, "Do you know what these are used for?"
The boy replied, "Not exactly, but they aren't for me. They're for him... He's my brother. He's four. We saw on TV that if you use these, you will be able to swim and ride a bike. Right now, he can't do either"
gist: A young boy buys tampons for his little brother because a TV ad promised they let you swim and ride a bike.

characters.looks: eight-year-old boy, earnest face, holding a box
small four-year-old boy, curious eyes, holding brother's hand
middle-aged pharmacist, white coat, raised eyebrows

text:
My ex just sneezed and I accidentally said "bless you"
Now she just staring at the bushes confused wondering who said that.
gist: A man says 'bless you' when his ex sneezes, revealing he is secretly hiding in the bushes near her.

characters.looks: man crouching in bushes, leaves in hair, binoculars
young woman with tissue, staring confused at bushes

text:
My 7 year old nephew showed me with pride the "telephone" he had just made from a string and two tin cans...
I pulled out my iPhone and said, "That's nice, but look at what kids your age make in China!"
gist: An uncle answers his nephew's homemade tin-can phone by showing a smartphone made by children his age in Chinese factories.

characters.looks: man in casual shirt, holding smartphone, smug grin
seven-year-old boy, proud smile, tin cans with string

text:
Two men are drinking in a bar
They pull out the sandwiches their wives had lovingly prepared and tuck in.
The bartender comes over and says "you can't eat your own food in here"
So they swapped sandwiches.
gist: Two men eating homemade sandwiches in a bar are told they cannot eat their own food, so they swap sandwiches.

characters.looks: two working men, flat caps, beer mugs
stern bartender, vest, wiping glass
